program_name: Analytics and Data Science for Economics and Management (ADSEM)
teaching_language: English. The programme is delivered entirely in English; all taught courses of both years are in English and the admission interview/test is also held in English.
campus: Brescia. Teaching and student services are based at the Department of Economics and Management (DEM), Via San Faustino 74/B, Brescia. [uncertain]
degree_class: LM-DATA (Data Science). The Italian/English title recorded in the official transparency data is 'Analytics e data science per l'economia e il management - Analytics and Data Science for Economics and Management (LM-Data)'. [uncertain]
english_delivery_scope: fully_english. The entire two-year, 120-ECTS master's degree is taught in English; there is no Italian-language curriculum or Italian-language track inside this degree, and English B2 is a formal admission prerequisite. No partial-English or curriculum-level split applies here (unlike the Management LM, where only some curricula are in English).
programme_status: active_first_year. The programme has been active since a.y. 2022/2023 and is admitting new first-year students for a.y. 2026/2027; admission tests for a.y. 2026/2027 are scheduled and the enrolling page publishes current-cycle requirements. Not phasing out, not under accreditation.
pre_evaluation_required: Yes, for candidates holding a foreign qualification. UNIBS requires international candidates applying to master's degrees to request pre-evaluation of their foreign degree and curriculum through the PICA online platform before enrolment. For open-access master's degrees in the Economics, Engineering and Law areas (which includes ADSEM, in the Economics area), pre-evaluation by the relevant Commission is compulsory for candidates with foreign degrees, in order to verify curricular requirements and personal preparation. A fee of EUR 20 is charged at the end of the PICA online procedure. Pre-evaluation runs in successive rounds: a first round reserved to non-EU citizens living abroad (also used for the LMINT and STAR PVS international scholarships), closing 15 March 2026 at noon Italian time, and further rounds open to EU and EU-equivalent citizens holding foreign degrees (pre-evaluation only, no scholarship) — for example the second round in the previous cycle ran from 30 June to 21 July at noon Italian time. [uncertain]
entry_test_name: There is no external or standardised admission test (no TOLC, no GMAT/GRE requirement, no SAT) for ADSEM. The internal instrument is an in-house 'admission test' / 'assessment of personal preparation' (verifica della preparazione personale) run by the programme's Selection Committee, consisting of an interview in English and/or a written test in English. It is a threshold/eligibility check rather than a ranked selective competition: candidates who satisfy the academic-record thresholds are exempted from it and admitted directly, and those who do not must sit and pass it. [uncertain]
admission_type: Open access (free/unrestricted access, 'accesso libero') with mandatory verification of curricular requirements and of personal preparation; no numerus clausus quota. Foreign-degree holders additionally go through the compulsory PICA pre-evaluation.
academic_requirements: Candidates must hold a bachelor's degree (laurea), a university diploma of at least three years' duration, or an equivalent foreign qualification recognised as suitable by the competent University bodies. Curricular requirement: at least 30 ECTS/CFU acquired in the previous university career in the following scientific-disciplinary sectors (SSD): INF/* (computer science), ING-INF/* (information engineering), MAT/* (mathematics), SECS-S/* (statistics and mathematical methods for economics), SECS-P/05 (econometrics), FIS/* (physics), MED/01 (medical statistics) and M-PSI/03 (psychometrics). A tolerance of six ECTS/CFU is allowed when verifying the minimum curricular requirement. Personal preparation: candidates who meet the curricular requirements are admitted directly (and exempted from the admission test) if they simultaneously satisfy the academic-record thresholds — a weighted average of examination marks of at least 24/30, an average mark of at least 24/30 in the exams belonging to the listed SSDs, and at least 44 CFU obtained in those SSDs. Candidates who do not meet all of these conditions are required by the Selection Committee to sit and pass the admission test. The assessment of personal competences and skills is based on the academic curriculum (weighted average mark of the examinations, average marks and number of CFU obtained in the courses falling within the specified fields, and consistency with the educational objectives of the course of study). For qualifications obtained abroad, the Course Council assesses the content of the completed study plan and the fulfilment of the disciplinary requirements; a candidate with a foreign qualification is considered eligible for the personal preparation assessment only if the first-level degree mark is at least 85/110 (or 77/100). Candidates who meet the requirements but have not yet graduated may pre-enrol 'in hypothesis' (conditional enrolment), which is void if the degree is not obtained in the examination sessions held by 31 December, considered extraordinary sessions of the previous academic year.
language_requirements: English proficiency at least at CEFR level B2 is a prerequisite for admission. It can be evidenced in any of the following alternative ways: (a) a B2-level certificate issued by the Language Teaching Centre (CLA) of the University of Brescia, or equivalent proof produced by a Language Centre or Language Service of an Italian or foreign university; (b) having acquired at least 3 CFU in English language teaching during previous university studies; or (c) having obtained a three-year degree (or equivalent qualification) with at least 60 CFU in educational activities carried out in English. No specific external test score (IELTS/TOEFL band) is stated as the sole accepted route on the official enrolling page; equivalent internationally recognised B2 certificates are handled through the equivalence route above. [uncertain]
application_deadline_eu: For EU/EU-equivalent and Italian candidates, enrolment in this open-access master's degree follows the annual Economics-area master's degree notice (Avviso LM Economia). Direct online admission/enrolment applications are accepted up to 31 December of the academic year concerned (late/'in-year' enrolment window; conditional enrolments lapse if the bachelor's degree is not obtained by that date). EU citizens holding a foreign qualification must in addition use the dedicated PICA pre-evaluation round for EU candidates (in the previous cycle: 30 June - 21 July at noon Italian time). Exact 2026/2027 dates must be read from the current Avviso. [uncertain]
application_deadline_non_eu: Non-EU candidates residing abroad: PICA pre-evaluation first round for a.y. 2026/2027 closes 15 March 2026 at noon (Italian time) — this round is also the one used for the LMINT and STAR PVS international scholarships. After receiving a positive pre-evaluation, non-EU candidates living abroad must submit and complete the pre-enrolment/study-visa application on the Universitaly portal by 31 August 2026, then complete matriculation at UNIBS after visa issuance and arrival. The Universitaly/visa step is separate from, and additional to, the UNIBS PICA pre-evaluation deadline. Non-EU candidates already legally resident in Italy follow the separate 'Non-EU candidates living in Italy: master's degrees' procedure and are not required to use Universitaly. [uncertain]
required_documents: For the PICA pre-evaluation and for the subsequent enrolment, foreign-qualification candidates must provide: the final diploma/degree certificate and the transcript of records in the original language, accompanied by an official translation into Italian or English (unless already issued in one of these languages), legalised or bearing the Apostille stamp issued by the authorities of the relevant educational system; the Declaration of Value (Dichiarazione di valore in loco) issued by the competent Italian diplomatic representation in the country of the education system attended, or an equivalent CIMEA statement of comparability where accepted; detailed syllabi/programmes of the examinations taken, bearing the foreign university stamp and translated into Italian or English (considered a preferential requirement); evidence of English proficiency at B2 (certificate, or transcript proof of at least 3 CFU of English, or of a degree with at least 60 CFU taught in English); a valid identity document/passport; and payment of the EUR 20 pre-evaluation fee. Italian-degree candidates submit their degree/transcript data through the university's online enrolment system. [uncertain]
entry_exam_or_test: Admission to the ADSEM master's degree by candidates who satisfy the minimum curricular requirements may take place only following an assessment of personal preparation carried out by a Selection Committee. The Committee first assesses the academic record (weighted average mark, average mark and number of CFU obtained in the listed SSDs, and consistency with the educational objectives of the programme). Candidates meeting the thresholds (weighted average at least 24/30; average at least 24/30 in the listed SSDs; at least 44 CFU in those SSDs) are admitted directly and exempted from the test. If the academic-record evaluation is not fully satisfactory, the candidate must pass an oral interview and/or a written test held in English. Candidates holding an Italian three-year university diploma and candidates holding a foreign degree are required to take this admission test. For foreign-degree holders, eligibility to sit the personal-preparation assessment requires a first-level degree mark of at least 85/110 (or 77/100). The test is not a competitive ranking exercise with a fixed number of places; it is a pass/fail eligibility check. Two test sittings are published for a.y. 2026/2027 in the Economics area: 1 July 2026 at 10:30 and 24 September 2026 at 10:30; a positive result is valid for admission to a.y. 2026/2027. [uncertain]
